docs.title: FingVibe user manual
docs.text:
Discover your local network. Understand and organize your devices.

FingVibe is a Windows 11 application. It scans your local network, shows devices that respond, and helps you organize them by person and room.

You do not need programming knowledge to use this manual. Start with Install and update, then follow Your first scan.

What would you like to do? Start here Get FingVibe Install, update, or remove the app Find devices Run your first scan Understand a result Device status, filters, and icons Organize equipment People and rooms Check a connection Network troubleshooting Understand privacy Network requests and local data

Native Windows screenshot with safe test data. It shows a test build, not a real home network. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: What this manual describes
docs.text:
This initial manual was checked against release v1.1.107 on 2026-11-09. It describes available behavior, not planned features. Your version is shown in Tools > About FingVibe.

Activity grids and the Completed Scan Observations table are temporarily unavailable in this version. First/last-seen summaries, saved scan evidence, and usage categories remain available. See History.

Select a screenshot to open it at full size. Screenshots may show a different test-build number. Their application source matches this release; sample values and test-only messages are not instructions.

A scan is a sample, not continuous monitoring

Online means a device responded in the displayed scan. Offline does not prove a device is turned off. An assigned device does not prove its owner is present. Only scan networks you own or have permission to inspect.

docs.title: Find help
docs.text:
Use the search box to find a term or task. On a small screen, open the menu, choose a section, then choose a chapter. Common problems gives practical checks before you report a bug.

Downloads, source code, and issue reports are available in the FingVibe repository.

docs.title: Build and contribute
docs.text: This is the smaller contributor section. App users can start with Install and update instead.

docs.title: Build prerequisites
docs.text:
Use Windows 11, the .NET 8 SDK, and Visual Studio 2022 with the Windows application development workload or equivalent Windows SDK tools. The desktop UI is native WinUI 3.

From the repository root:

dotnet restore FingVibe.sln
dotnet run --project src\FingVibe.App\FingVibe.App.csproj -p:Platform=x64

Official app downloads are self-contained; these prerequisites are for source builds. The optional speed-test host uses WebView2, not a web-based app shell.

docs.title: Component boundaries
docs.text:
Component Responsibility Application shell Initialization, routing, shared header, and top-level wiring. Page views Visual trees, local layout/state, and focused UI request events. Scan execution/scheduling Serialized network activity, manual/scheduled outcomes, timing, and lifecycle. Scanner and enrichment Probe orchestration and evidence for names, vendors, ports, and classification. Core/storage Models, evidence rules, transactional inventory, and bounded history queries.

Keep page-specific behavior with its owning module. Coordinate shared-contract changes before editing. The complete ownership list and review expectations remain in CONTRIBUTING.

docs.title: Validate relevant behavior
docs.text:
For WinUI-free Core coverage:

dotnet test tests\FingVibe.Core.Tests\FingVibe.Core.Tests.csproj --configuration Release

Use the smallest relevant existing checks for a focused change. Native UI coverage requires a disposable, usable Windows desktop. Do not move the pointer, send keyboard input, or change accessibility settings on the user's working desktop to run regression tests.

Current checks, capture mappings, build identity, and CI gates are recorded in the test reference. Pending independent validation work is not described here as delivered.

docs.title: Submit a focused change
docs.text:
Read existing instructions and issue scope before changing code. Keep unrelated formatting and cleanup out of feature PRs. Update directly related documentation and regression coverage.

Issue intake, Epic organization, readiness, and agent ownership follow the development backlog contract. Labels and Epic membership are not implementation approval.

Build identifiers distinguish local, PR, test, and official release artifacts. Merging to main can trigger existing release automation. This documentation workflow does not change app builds, release gates, branch protection, or merge authority.

docs.title: Saved data and backups
docs.text:
FingVibe saves data under:

%LOCALAPPDATA%\FingVibe

Press Win+R, enter that path, and press Enter to open the folder. It is different from the installer folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\FingVibe.

docs.title: Important files
docs.text:
File Purpose device-inventory.sqlite Authoritative inventory, names, identification corrections, people/rooms, assignments, virtual identities, history, and discovery baselines. latest-scan.json Separate saved-scan cache. SQLite checkpoints are authoritative when present. appearance.json Appearance choices. device-table.json Column choices, widths, row density, previews, and Status filtering. navigation.json Wide-window navigation width/collapse preferences. periodic-scan.json Scheduled-scan choice and interval. router-wan.json Optional WAN values by Windows network profile.

The folder can also contain cached vendor registries and older migration inputs. Do not edit the SQLite database or remove individual records with another tool as a normal way to change app data. Use FingVibe's own editors.

docs.title: Make a backup
docs.text:
There is no automatic backup feature in the version covered by this manual. Make a manual copy:

  1. Close all FingVibe instances.
  2. Wait until the app has finished closing.
  3. Open %LOCALAPPDATA%\FingVibe.
  4. Copy the whole folder to a separate, dated backup location.
  5. Keep the copy private.

Copying the whole folder preserves database sidecar files if any remain, as well as preferences. Do not copy only an open database while the app is saving. The SQL editor's report output is not a complete backup.

History is retained without automatic age/count trimming. The database and backups can grow over time.

docs.title: Restore a backup
docs.text:
1. Close all FingVibe instances.
  2. Make a separate copy of the current data folder first.
  3. Move the current folder aside rather than merging files into it.
  4. Restore the complete backup as %LOCALAPPDATA%\FingVibe.
  5. Start a compatible current FingVibe release.
  6. Check saved names, assignments, and preferences.
  7. Run a new scan when you need current presence evidence.

Restoration replaces the saved state with the backup's state. It does not merge later edits into an older copy. Historical results are not live Online evidence. If the restored database cannot be loaded, stop and keep both copies for diagnosis.

docs.title: Older JSON files
docs.text:
Earlier versions stored inventory and metadata in JSON. Supported legacy files are migration input, not synchronized copies of SQLite. Original legacy files are left intact during migration.

Once SQLite is authoritative, editing old JSON does not update the app. An invalid existing SQLite database does not safely fall back to stale JSON. See Common problems.

docs.title: Remove saved data
docs.text:
This removes your saved state

Removing this folder discards inventory, history, names, corrections, people/rooms, assignments, and preferences. Make a backup first.

  1. Close all FingVibe instances.
  2. Make a backup if you might need the data again.
  3. Remove or move aside only %LOCALAPPDATA%\FingVibe.
  4. Start FingVibe to create a new saved state.

Do not remove the broader %LOCALAPPDATA% directory. Uninstalling the app alone preserves this separate data folder.

For errors, preserve the affected files before trying recovery. Do not delete a damaged database just to hide the error.

docs.title: Identify and inspect a device
docs.text:
Select a row on Devices to open its details. Use the Devices return action when finished.

Native test-build screenshot. The hostname belongs to the disposable CI runner; addresses and metadata are safe review data. Lower sections require scrolling. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: Understand identification
docs.text:
Network overview shows the observed address, MAC address, hostname, vendor, and available response measurements. Device identification shows the type, operating system, brand, family, model, and selected icon.

FingVibe gathers local name and service evidence. It can also use a MAC prefix to find the registered vendor. This does not reliably identify every device.

(likely) means the evidence suggests a classification but does not prove it. Unknown is an intentional result when evidence is absent or conflicting. Open How this device was identified to see why a value was selected. Running a web server or file-sharing service alone does not identify the OS.

docs.title: Rename
docs.text:
1. Choose Rename near the device name.
  2. Enter your preferred name.
  3. Choose Save.
  4. Check the save feedback.
  5. Choose Done to close the editor.

A saved name is separate from the discovered hostname. Choose Use imported / discovered name to remove your custom name. Closing the editor is not a substitute for checking whether a save succeeded.

docs.title: Correct identification
docs.text:
1. Find Device identification.
  2. Choose Edit.
  3. Change the type, OS, brand, family, model, or icon.
  4. Choose Save changes, or Cancel to discard the draft.

Your saved corrections take precedence over imported values and automatic evidence. Blank brand/family/model fields inherit their original/default values. Automatic uses automatic evidence when there is no mapped Fing value; an imported option explicitly says it uses imported Fing OS/type.

Reset saved identification clears the six identification overrides. It does not remove the device name, assignments, or original imported evidence. An error leaves the draft visible so you can review it.

Names and corrections normally follow the device's MAC address, not its IP. A changing MAC can break that association.

docs.title: Inspect services
docs.text:
The normal LAN scan checks ten common TCP ports. For a currently responding address, Scan additional ports checks a curated set of 100 additional TCP ports.

  1. Confirm the device responded in the current local scan.
  2. If several current addresses exist, select Current address to inspect / probe.
  3. Review Ports & services.
  4. Optionally select Include UDP service checks.
  5. Choose Scan additional ports.
  6. Read the outcome and endpoint details.

UDP service checks cover a small supported set, not every UDP port. No response is inconclusive; it is not proof that a UDP port is open or closed. Do not run probes against historical imported addresses. The app prevents conflicting network measurements from running together.

Copy controls appear beside populated values on hover or keyboard focus. Copy only information you intend to share; MACs, names, and addresses can be private.

docs.title: Assign equipment
docs.text:
Choose a Person and Room in Assignments. Each selection saves when changed; the categories are independent. See People and rooms.

Usage category has a separate draft and save action. Changing that draft does not save it through the Person/Room controls. See Usage categories.

docs.title: Virtual-device details
docs.text:
For an inferred virtual identity, names, corrections, and assignments belong to that identity and can follow its associated MAC changes.

Expand MAC and address history for the member addresses, times, and preserved evidence. Do not treat this association as proof of a physical device. Fing import still matches full MAC addresses, not virtual names or prefixes.

docs.title: History availability
docs.text: First/last-seen and last-observed summaries are available. Activity grids and the Completed Scan Observations table are temporarily hidden in the initial manual's release. There is no setting to enable them. See History and usage categories.

docs.title: Understand device results
docs.text: Devices is a persistent inventory: a saved list of known devices. It includes local observations and devices imported from Fing. Unused IP addresses do not become device records.

docs.title: Device status
docs.text:
Status Meaning Online The device responded to fresh ping or ARP in this session's displayed scan. Initial saved results can show this while background checks continue. Offline A previously observed device did not respond in a later successful scan of the same identified network and subnet. Unknown There is no suitable current scan evidence, for example after restart or when results belong to another network. Fing Only The imported MAC address has never been observed in a local FingVibe scan.

Offline is not proof of power-off. A device may be sleeping, blocking probes, or outside the scan's reachable network. After restart, saved observations are historical; they do not remain Online.

Color supports the status text. Green, gray, or amber alone is not the meaning. The totals describe the whole inventory, even when filters hide some rows.

docs.title: Search and filter
docs.text:
1. Enter a name, address, vendor, or other displayed information in Search devices.
  2. Open Status to choose one or more statuses.
  3. Choose the funnel icon to show more filters.
  4. Select values in Device type, Operating system, Vendor, Person, Room, Ports, or Usage category.
  5. Choose Clear filters beside the funnel to remove all restrictions.

Selecting several values within one category means "any of these." Different categories combine: a device must match each selected category and the search text. An empty selection means no restriction.

For example, select Online, a room, and With open ports to see responding devices in that room with observed services. Unassigned finds devices with no person or room. Unknown type or OS finds devices without that classification.

Hiding the second filter row does not clear it. The funnel count shows active secondary categories. Status is remembered after restart; search and the other categories are not.

The sample search matches no device. It does not mean the inventory is empty. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: Sort and resize
docs.text:
Choose a column heading to sort ascending. Choose it again to reverse the order. Combined columns keep separate heading actions for their fields. Person and Room sort by full name, not by the short label.

Drag a column boundary to resize it. Use Settings to show, hide, or combine columns. Name and IP address always remain visible.

docs.title: Response times and service icons
docs.text:
Response time is the measured ping delay in milliseconds (ms). A smaller value means that ping returned faster, not that the device's internet connection is faster. The response bars share one scale for the displayed scan. Filtering does not change that scale.

Service icons represent observed ports, such as a web or file-sharing service. Hover over an icon for the port number and name. An open port is not a security verdict. It does not prove a service is safe, unsafe, or running a particular operating system.

docs.title: Last seen
docs.text:
Last seen shows the latest local presence evidence for the selected network. Online in that column describes the displayed scan. A relative age, such as 2 h ago, describes saved evidence.

Never means an imported-only device has not been seen by a local scan. Unavailable means suitable evidence is missing or cannot be read. Hover or focus the value to see its exact time or explanation. Age text refreshes while Devices is open; it does not run another scan.

docs.title: Private and virtual devices
docs.text:
Private MAC means a locally administered MAC address. It is not a known manufacturer and does not prove that an address changes randomly. Private as a vendor can mean an undisclosed IEEE registrant.

A multiple-PC icon can mark a virtual device: FingVibe's inferred identity for certain sparse private-prefix observations across changing MAC addresses. It does not mean a virtual machine. The association is an estimate, not proof that several observations belong to one physical device. See Device details.

docs.title: Maintain this documentation
docs.text:
The website is built with MkDocs 1.6.1 and Material 9.6.22. Markdown in docs/index.md and docs/manual/ is its single authored source. Images live under docs/screenshots/manual/; the logo is an existing branding asset. One small theme partial keeps the source link static instead of fetching GitHub repository statistics. Fonts and search assets are served locally.

Existing technical references, archived designs, agent prompts, and backlog contracts remain in the repository. They are deliberately not website chapters. Links to them open their GitHub source.

docs.title: Build locally
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12 and run these commands from the repository root. A virtual environment keeps documentation dependencies separate:

python -m venv .venv-docs
.\.venv-docs\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements-docs.txt
.\.venv-docs\Scripts\python.exe tests\Documentation.Tests.py
.\.venv-docs\Scripts\python.exe tests\DocumentationPublish.Tests.py
.\.venv-docs\Scripts\python.exe -m mkdocs build --strict
.\.venv-docs\Scripts\python.exe tools\Check-Documentation.py site

The generated output is site/, which is ignored by Git. Do not commit it. For a local preview:

.\.venv-docs\Scripts\python.exe -m mkdocs serve

Open the local URL printed by MkDocs. Stop the server when finished. The website is separate from the native WinUI application.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
The Documentation workflow builds changed documentation on pull requests. It checks links, fragments, assets, image alternative text, decorative icon accessibility, and search output before uploading a Pages artifact. Pull requests and feature-branch manual runs do not deploy. Publisher regression tests verify archive preservation, bounded file ownership, stale-file cleanup, unsafe-path rejection, and repeat publication.

After a matching push to main, the deployment job publishes the checked artifact to GitHub Pages. A manual workflow run on main can republish it without changing app releases. The main-only publication job has narrowly scoped contents/Pages write permissions so it can update the existing publishing branch and request a build.

The repository already publishes native PR screenshots under ui-review/ on the gh-pages branch. Documentation shares that branch without replacing this archive. A manifest tracks only documentation-owned files so obsolete manual files can be removed without deleting screenshots or unrelated content. Concurrent branch updates are rebased before a bounded push retry.

Keep Settings > Pages > Source: Deploy from a branch, using gh-pages and its root folder. The github-pages environment must allow main for the publishing job; its existing gh-pages allowance is preserved. The job explicitly requests a Pages build after publication, rather than relying on a token-generated push to trigger another workflow. Existing screenshot publishing remains unchanged. These settings do not change application release policy or branch protection.

A successful PR build is not proof that the live site was deployed. After publication, the main job waits for the Pages build and verifies the live revision marker, manual homepage, local search data, and all thirteen new images. After merge, check that result and the real /fingvibe/ project URL. Inspect interactive search and navigation there too.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
Use short sentences and familiar words for non-native speakers. Explain a technical term when it first appears. Use exact UI labels and one action per numbered step. Describe the expected result and keep warnings beside risky actions.

Keep detailed implementation/test internals in contributor or technical records. Avoid idioms, decorative jargon, and claims of continuous presence. When behavior changes, update related pages together and update the homepage's release baseline after verification.

docs.title: Images and icons
docs.text:
Reuse meaningful app imagery where possible. Keep text beside icons and provide descriptive alternative text for screenshots. Decorative SVGs should be hidden from assistive technology, not announced repeatedly.

Use privacy-safe native screenshots, never an unredacted real inventory. Record source revision, run, test identity, dimensions, edits, and visible state in Screenshot sources. Do not imply that a ready-state capture shows real measured results.

Do not obtain fresh screenshots by automating a working user's desktop. Use existing disposable Windows CI capture tooling.

docs.title: Related work
docs.text: #253 owns the separate documentation refresh/audit-agent request. This site adds no agent or schedule. Shared technical/contributor documentation and Activity restoration can evolve independently; reconcile their released behavior before changing user instructions.

docs.title: Your first scan
docs.text: A LAN is a local area network, such as the devices connected to your home router. FingVibe scans IPv4 addresses on the network you select.

docs.title: Choose the network
docs.text:
1. Connect your PC to the network you want to inspect.
  2. Open FingVibe.
  3. Open Devices from the left menu.
  4. Open the shared Network: picker near the top.
  5. Select the Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection you want to scan.

The picker shows the adapter and its network range, for example 192.168.1.0/24. If you are unsure which adapter to use, compare it with your active connection in Windows network settings.

Do not choose a VPN or virtual adapter just because it appears first. Only scan a network you own or have permission to inspect.

docs.title: Run the scan
docs.text:
1. Choose Scan LAN on Devices.
  2. Watch the progress and status beneath the network picker.
  3. Wait for the scan to finish, or choose Cancel scan to stop it.
  4. Select a device row to inspect the result.

Initial results become available before the background checks finish. You can browse and filter them while those checks continue. Cancel scan remains available if you visit another page.

Safe loopback test data. This capture was taken after a cancellation test; the retained-result message is intentional. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: What happens during a scan
docs.text:
FingVibe first sends ping requests to usable addresses. A ping asks a device for a small response. It then uses fresh ARP checks for addresses that did not answer. ARP asks for an address match on the directly connected network.

If unconfirmed addresses remain, FingVibe waits ten seconds and tries ping again. It can wait another ten seconds before the final ping attempt. An address has at most three ping attempts and one fresh ARP check. Devices already confirmed are not retried.

The later stages can take longer than the first results. A mostly silent network can take more than twenty extra seconds, plus probe and save time. The selected network cannot silently change to a different network mid-scan.

docs.title: Read the result safely
docs.text:
Online means a fresh ping or ARP response in the displayed scan. An ARP-only response may have no ping response time; that is not an error.

Some active devices do not answer either check. Firewalls, sleeping devices, guest-network isolation, and network configuration can affect discovery. Two scans do not have to find the same number of devices.

FingVibe retains previously known and imported devices. The number of rows in Devices is therefore not always the number that answered the latest scan. See Device status.

docs.title: Cancel, fail, or change networks
docs.text:
Before the first saved checkpoint, cancellation or failure leaves the old displayed results unchanged. After a checkpoint, FingVibe keeps the saved observations but marks the scan incomplete. It does not mark missing devices Offline from an incomplete scan.

Selecting another network does not turn old results into results for the new network. Check the displayed subnet and freshness message before interpreting the list. Run a new scan when you need observations for the selected network.

If the app reports a save error, do not assume the results were saved. See Common problems.

docs.title: Terms and icons
docs.text: Use these short explanations when a network term or visual hint is unfamiliar.

docs.title: Network terms
docs.text: Term Plain-English meaning LAN Local area network, such as equipment connected through your home router. Adapter A Windows network connection, such as Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or a virtual interface. IPv4 / IP address An address such as 192.168.1.20. It can change and is not permanent device identity. Subnet / prefix A network range. /24 indicates how much of the IPv4 address belongs to its network portion. MAC address A link-layer address, usually six bytes such as 02-00-00-00-00-01. Some devices change it. ARP A local IPv4 address-resolution request. A fresh response can confirm a device without a ping reply. ICMP / ping A small network request that can measure a response; not every device answers. Gateway The router/address used to reach destinations outside the local subnet. DNS A service that resolves names, such as example.com, to addresses. TCP / UDP Two transport protocols used by services. Silent UDP results are inconclusive. Port A numbered service endpoint, such as TCP 443. An open port is not a security verdict. ISP Internet service provider. Public-IP lookup can identify a provider approximately. WAN The internet-facing side of a router or network. VPN A virtual private network; it can change Windows routing and visible addresses. ms Milliseconds, used for response delays. Mbps Megabits per second, used for internet bandwidth measurements. Snapshot / checkpoint Saved scan state. An incomplete checkpoint is not a completed scan. SQLite / SQL The local database format / language used to query saved data.

docs.title: Visual hints
docs.text:
The website uses locally served SVG icons from the documentation theme. They help scan a page but do not replace text. The Windows app uses its own native glyphs.

Visual Meaning and limitation Scan hint Look for Scan LAN. The website glyph is not an app button. Funnel Show or hide more filters. Hidden restrictions still apply. Copy Copy the associated value. Check privacy before sharing it. Edit Change the associated saved information. Read the page's save behavior. Person A manual equipment assignment, not proof of presence. Room A manual location label, not a physical location measurement. Multiple-PC app icon An inferred virtual identity; not necessarily a virtual machine. Colored status dot Supports Online/Offline/Unknown/Fing Only text. Color alone is not evidence. Service app icon An observed port/service. Hover for its number and name.

(likely) signals uncertainty. Unavailable signals missing or unreadable information. Neither should be replaced with an assumed fact.

docs.title: History and usage categories
docs.text: FingVibe saves scan evidence. Evidence describes what a scan observed, not uninterrupted device availability or human presence.

docs.title: First seen, last seen, and last observed
docs.text:
Open a device's details and find its Scan history summary. The summary uses the selected Windows network identity and subnet.

Value Meaning First seen Earliest suitable saved local presence observation. Last seen Latest suitable saved local presence observation. Missing responses do not advance it. Last observed: Present/Absent The state in the relevant recorded scan, not live status. Observed online/offline since The first recorded scan in the latest sequence of that state. Gaps between scans are not continuous evidence.

Times are displayed in local time. Full timestamps include the UTC offset where available. A restart preserves history but does not make it current. Imported Fing times do not create local presence or invented scan rows.

Changing networks does not substitute another network's history. An unavailable value may mean the selected context has no suitable evidence. The Devices Last seen column uses the same scope.

docs.title: Temporarily unavailable controls
docs.text:
In release v1.1.107, the Activity grid and Completed Scan Observations expander/table are hidden. They have no user-facing enable switch.

The app still retains scan evidence and displays the summary. This manual does not give steps for controls you cannot use. Their restoration is tracked separately in #273 and #274. Check your release notes before following instructions for a later version.

docs.title: Usage categories
docs.text:
The Usage category column can show:

Category Automatic rule Permanent The device responded in at least 80% of eligible scans. Guest The device responded in at most 10% of eligible scans. Personal Other devices may qualify when overnight/weekend response is at least 60% and at least 20 percentage points above weekday daytime, with evidence in both groups. Unclassified No eligible evidence, or none of the other rules applies.

Rules run in that order. They use today and the previous six local dates on the selected network, bounded by the device's first reliable sighting. Overnight is 18:00-06:00; weekends also belong to that comparison group.

Limited evidence means the result is based on too few dates or scans to meet the app's evidence thresholds. The category may still appear. For example, 12 responses out of 14 eligible scans can suggest Permanent, but with limited evidence.

Incomplete scans, imported totals, unknown gaps, and unrelated networks do not become nonresponses. The time of day you scan affects the recommendation. Guest does not prove a visitor, and Personal does not prove ownership.

docs.title: Set a category yourself
docs.text:
1. Open the device's details.
  2. Find Usage category in Assignments.
  3. Choose the category you want.
  4. Choose Save category.
  5. Use Cancel to discard an unsaved category change.

Choose Automatic and save to remove your override. The recommendation and its counts remain visible for comparison.

This save is independent of Person and Room, which save when changed. A save error retains the category draft. If another app instance changed the data, Reload saved category discards the draft and loads the saved value before you try again.

There is no screenshot of the hidden Activity/table controls in this manual. This avoids illustrating unavailable features as usable.

docs.title: Import from Fing
docs.text: Use Tools > Import from Fing to bring device information from a Fing Excel export into FingVibe. You review changes before saving them. Analysis alone does not change the inventory.

docs.title: Prepare the export
docs.text:
Open How to export your devices from Fing for guidance. Export menus and availability depend on your Fing version and subscription.

Use a local .xlsx workbook with a Devices sheet and a MAC header. CSV, PDF, and arbitrary spreadsheets are not supported.

Supported optional columns include Name, Hostname, Type, Brand, Family, Model, OS, OS Version, Owner, Location, and IP. The limits are 10 MB compressed, 64 MB uncompressed, and 20,000 device rows. Spreadsheet formulas are not executed.

docs.title: Analyze
docs.text:
1. Open Tools > Import from Fing.
  2. Choose Browse..., or drag the workbook into the file area.
  3. Read the Analysis groups.
  4. Resolve missing or ambiguous people/rooms using their management pages.
  5. Return and choose Analyze again.

Synthetic export, not a real workbook. The green filename means analysis succeeded; it does not approve every proposed change. Screenshot sources.

Owner and Location match the full names of existing People and Rooms. Matching ignores letter case and surrounding spaces, but needs exactly one match. Import never creates people or rooms automatically.

Invalid MACs and all rows sharing a duplicate MAC are skipped with warnings. A valid private/randomized MAC can be imported, but its long-term identity may be uncertain.

docs.title: Review conflicts
docs.text:
Find Changes and conflicts and review each device. Existing customizations are kept by default. Choose Replace only for a field you want to overwrite. Empty imported fields do not erase saved information.

For example, if your saved name is Kitchen printer and the workbook has HP printer, keep the saved name unless you intentionally want the replacement.

Manual identification corrections take precedence over imported classification. Detailed original Fing values remain available in device details. Unknown or uncertain mappings are not treated as proven classifications.

docs.title: Import the reviewed devices
docs.text:
Use Import device for one device or Import all for all eligible changes. For a subset:

  1. Choose Select devices.
  2. Check the devices you recognize.
  3. Review your keep/replace decisions.
  4. Choose Import selected (N).
  5. Check Imported this session and any remaining preview items.

Selection starts empty. Import all does not automatically approve overwrites; every save respects your field choices. Each requested batch saves completely or not at all. An error must not be treated as a partially successful import.

Changing the file or relevant saved data can invalidate the preview. If the file changed or another app instance saved newer data, analyze again.

docs.title: Understand the result
docs.text:
Devices are matched by full MAC address, not IP. Fing Only means no local FingVibe observation exists for that MAC. The exported IP is historical context; it does not establish Online status or authorize probing that address.

Import does not migrate Fing events, timestamps, or presence. For precise format and precedence details, see the technical import reference.

docs.title: Install and update
docs.text: Choose the installer for a normal installation, or the ZIP for a portable copy.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
FingVibe supports Windows 11 on an x64 PC. Official downloads include the .NET components needed by the app. You do not need the .NET SDK or Visual Studio unless you want to build FingVibe from source.

The optional speed test needs Microsoft Edge WebView2. If it cannot start, see Speed test problems.

docs.title: Install FingVibe
docs.text:
1. Open the latest release.
  2. Download FingVibe-<version>-win-x64-Setup.exe.
  3. Close any running copy of FingVibe.
  4. Run the installer.
  5. Open FingVibe from the Start menu.

The installer installs the app for your Windows user. It does not need administrator rights. Its default app folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\FingVibe.

Unsigned download

FingVibe downloads are unsigned. Windows may show an unknown-publisher or SmartScreen warning. Check that the file came from the repository's official release page before deciding whether to run it. Do not disable Windows security or ignore a warning for an untrusted download.

After launch, follow Your first scan.

docs.title: Use the portable ZIP
docs.text:
1. Download FingVibe-<version>-win-x64.zip from the release page.
  2. Extract the ZIP into a new folder.
  3. Open that folder.
  4. Run FingVibe.App.exe.

Keep all extracted files together. Do not run the executable from inside the ZIP or copy only the executable to another folder.

"Portable" describes the app files. Your saved data still lives under your Windows user profile, not beside the executable. Installed and portable copies use the same data folder for that user.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
FingVibe does not automatically install a new release.

  1. Check the release page.
  2. Make a backup before an important update.
  3. Close all running copies of FingVibe.
  4. For an installed copy, run the newer installer.
  5. For a portable copy, extract the new ZIP into a fresh folder.
  6. Start the updated app.
  7. Check Tools > About FingVibe for the expected version.

The app upgrades supported saved data when needed. The installer rejects downgrades. Older app builds may not understand the current database; do not use an old build as a way to undo a data upgrade.

docs.title: Remove the app
docs.text:
For an installed copy, open Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find FingVibe, and choose Uninstall after closing the app.

For a portable copy, close FingVibe and remove its extracted app folder.

Removing the application does not remove the separate saved-data folder. To remove your data as well, follow Remove saved data.

docs.title: Find your way around
docs.text:
The left menu switches pages. The Network: picker and scan status are shared across pages. Changing pages does not automatically start another scan.

Page What it is for Overview Read the displayed scan summary and open its device results. Network See local addressing, network size, and available public-IP/provider details. Devices Browse the persistent device inventory and start a LAN scan. People Create people and manage equipment assignments. Rooms Create rooms and organize equipment by location. Tools Open import, SQL reports, diagnostics, speed test, and About. Settings Change appearance, device-table options, and scheduled scans.

These manual icons are visual hints, not exact copies of every Windows glyph. The text labels remain the instructions.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Overview describes the displayed scan, not a live network monitor. Choose an online-device or open-port summary to open the corresponding Devices results. These shortcuts clear older search and filter restrictions.

A card's subnet size describes address capacity, not how many devices are connected. Before your first scan, follow the scan guidance rather than treating unknown counts as measurements.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
The public address, provider, location, and loopback network are safe examples, not measurements of the user's connection. Screenshot sources.

The Machine IPv4 address is this PC's address on the selected network. The LAN address includes the subnet prefix, such as /24. The Public IP address is the address internet services see.

Public-IP, provider, and approximate location information needs internet access. It can be unavailable while LAN scanning still works. The reported location is not a precise physical location. See Privacy.

The scanner accepts at most 65,534 usable addresses in a target. A larger network-size explanation does not remove that safety limit.

docs.title: Resize the menu
docs.text:
Drag the menu's right edge to change its width. A narrow menu becomes an icon rail. Use the menu button to reopen the labels. Wide-window width and collapse choices are remembered; automatic changes for a small window are not.

You can focus the divider and use Left/Right arrow keys. Hold Shift for larger steps. Small windows may show an overlay menu.

docs.title: Return and use the keyboard
docs.text:
Device details has a Devices return action. Individual Tools pages have a Tools return action. These return to the relevant page; they do not save an unfinished draft unless the page explicitly says so.

Use Tab to move through controls, and Enter or Space to activate the focused control. Checkboxes expose their selected state. Tooltips and accessible names provide full values when table text is shortened.

docs.title: Network troubleshooting
docs.text: Use Tools > Network troubleshooting to run connection checks manually. Opening the page does not send diagnostic probes.

docs.title: Run checks
docs.text:
1. Open Tools > Network troubleshooting.
  2. Review the LAN adapter context.
  3. Use Refresh adapters if your connection changed.
  4. Leave the optional router WAN address blank unless you know it.
  5. Read What these checks send.
  6. Choose Run checks.
  7. Read each checkpoint and the traceroute result.

Safe UI-review ready state. Review mode disables actual diagnostic probes. That test-only restriction does not apply to a normal release. Screenshot sources.

Cancel, leaving the page, changing its network context, or closing the app stops the checks. A LAN scan, speed test, or device-service probe must finish before another network measurement can start.

docs.title: What is checked
docs.text:
Check What a response can tell you Loopback 127.0.0.1 This PC's local network stack answered. This PC's LAN IPv4 The selected local address answered. Gateway The configured router/local gateway answered, if available. Optional router WAN The supplied address answered; it may not answer ping. 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 The public targets answered the requested IP check. DNS Name resolution for example.com succeeded through the tested resolver. Traceroute Some routers on the route toward 1.1.1.1 returned hop information.

DNS translates a name into an address. Traceroute asks for responses at successive routing steps. Some routers do not answer these probes, even when they forward normal traffic. An unanswered hop does not by itself locate a connection fault.

The checks use short timeouts. Traceroute stops after at most sixteen hops. A completely unanswered run takes about 38 seconds plus Windows scheduling time.

Windows selects the actual routing and DNS context. Choosing an adapter here does not bind all public checks to that adapter. VPNs and multiple adapters can change the route.

docs.title: Router WAN address
docs.text:
WAN means the router's internet-facing side. The WAN IPv4 may differ from the public address seen by a website, for example with provider-side address sharing.

  1. Open your router's administration page in a browser.
  2. Sign in there, not in FingVibe.
  3. Find Internet, WAN, or Status.
  4. Copy the WAN/Internet IPv4 address into the optional field.

Never enter router credentials into FingVibe. Leaving the field blank is valid. A valid edit saves for the current Windows network profile; clearing it removes that profile's saved value. The address may change later.

docs.title: Read the diagram
docs.text:
The diagram organizes logical checks. It is not a discovered physical network map and does not prove that devices are directly connected to one another. Read each label and status rather than interpreting colored lines alone.

Earlier user-supplied ready-state screenshot, with approved address redactions. No checks had run. Its exact application revision is unknown. Screenshot sources.

Public targets receive your public source address and relevant DNS query. See Privacy and Common problems.

docs.title: People and rooms
docs.text: Use People and Rooms to label who uses equipment and where it belongs. FingVibe does not automatically discover a device's owner or room.

docs.title: Create a person or room
docs.text:
1. Open People or Rooms.
  2. Choose Add person or Add room.
  3. Enter the full name.
  4. Review the suggested short name.
  5. Optionally choose an icon and enter notes.
  6. Save the entry.

Short names contain one to three visible characters and must be unique within People or within Rooms. For example, Living Room can use LR. Editing a suggested short name stops its automatic updates.

The person is a synthetic test entry, not a real user. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: Assign devices
docs.text:
From Devices:

  1. Select the device.
  2. Find Assignments.
  3. Choose a Person.
  4. Choose a Room if needed.
  5. Check any save feedback.

Person and Room save independently when changed. Either can be Unassigned. You can also open a person or room's details and choose Assign devices.

This example has no assigned devices. The response count is not a presence measurement for a person. Screenshot sources.

Assignments normally need a valid six-byte MAC address. They do not follow an IP address alone. Randomized or changing MACs can lose the link; supported inferred virtual identities keep their own assignments.

docs.title: Find, edit, or delete
docs.text:
Search the People or Rooms page by name. Open an entry to review its assigned equipment. Use its edit action to change the name, icon, or notes.

Deleting a person clears that person's device assignments. Deleting a room clears only that room's assignments. Neither action deletes devices or scan history.

The Devices table can show short Person and Room labels. Their tooltips give the full names. Filters and search also match full names.

docs.title: Interpret counts
docs.text:
Last scan counts devices that responded in the displayed local scan. It does not show whether a person is home, a room is occupied, or a device is continuously connected.

Your entries and assignments are saved locally. If a load or save fails, read the error before making further changes. See Saved data.

docs.title: Privacy and network requests
docs.text: FingVibe keeps its inventory, names, assignments, and saved scans on your PC. Local discovery is not a cloud inventory upload. Some features contact external services as explained below.

docs.title: Requests by feature
docs.text:
Feature Where requests go Information involved LAN discovery and identification Devices on the selected local network Ping, fresh ARP, name/service discovery, and bounded service probes. MAC vendor lookup Official IEEE registries Registry downloads, cached locally for 30 days. No inventory upload is needed. Public IP/provider details ipwho.is Your public source IP; the service returns provider and approximate location information. Configured provider logos Logo.dev Provider name and your public source IP, not LAN inventory or scan results. Speed test speed.cloudflare.com Measurement traffic, public source IP, and default engine result reporting after per-run confirmation. Network troubleshooting Local checkpoints, public IP targets, and DNS resolvers Ping/traceroute traffic and DNS queries for example.com. Links opened from the app Your external browser Normal requests to the selected website.

Public lookup and provider logos are optional displays. Missing configuration or service failure does not prevent local scanning. The speed test is manual and asks for confirmation before each run. Troubleshooting probes start only when you choose Run checks.

docs.title: Understand public addresses
docs.text:
An internet service normally sees your connection's public source IP. That may belong to a VPN or provider gateway rather than this PC's LAN address. Approximate public-IP location is not a reliable physical location.

Windows controls routing for internet measurements. A selected LAN adapter does not guarantee that a VPN is bypassed.

docs.title: Saved data
docs.text:
Your saved data can include device names, full MAC/IP addresses, people/room names and notes, assignments, network identities, and observation times. Treat the data folder and backups as private.

The app does not establish human presence, continuous uptime, or a physical network map from these observations. Keeping data local does not make a shared screenshot or backup harmless.

docs.title: Share screenshots safely
docs.text:
Before posting a screenshot or log:

  1. Check every visible name, address, MAC, note, and hostname.
  2. Remove or redact private values, including repeated values in diagrams.
  3. Keep error text and build identity useful for diagnosis.
  4. Say when values or results are sample data.

Do not post router credentials, provider credentials, connection strings, private Fing workbooks, or a complete inventory database. Use Version and support for a safe bug-report checklist.

The documentation website uses locally served fonts, scripts, search data, screenshots, and icons. It includes no analytics configuration. Following an external link still contacts that external website.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: Start with the visible error or status message. Avoid changing several settings at once; one change at a time makes the result easier to understand.

docs.title: Fewer devices than expected
docs.text:
1. Check the selected Wi-Fi/Ethernet adapter and subnet.
  2. Wait for the full scan, including background checks, to finish.
  3. Clear Devices filters.
  4. Check whether missing devices are asleep or on another network.
  5. Check guest-network/client-isolation settings if you manage the router.
  6. Run another scan and compare device identities, not only totals.

Active devices can ignore ping and ARP. A different application's device count is not proof that every missing device should answer FingVibe. Saved and imported devices also affect inventory totals.

Only change firewall or router settings when you understand the effect and have permission. Do not disable the firewall as a general fix.

docs.title: No usable network or the wrong network
docs.text:
Check Windows connection status. VPN, Hyper-V, and other virtual adapters can appear alongside physical connections. Select the intended directly connected IPv4 network.

In troubleshooting, use Refresh adapters after changes. A VPN can still affect internet routes even when the LAN picker is correct. Large scan ranges may exceed the 65,534-address limit. IPv6-only device discovery is outside this scanner's current IPv4 scope.

docs.title: Empty Devices list
docs.text:
Read Showing N of M devices. If the inventory has devices but zero are shown, use Clear filters. Hidden secondary filters still apply.

A remembered Status: Online filter may show no rows after restart because saved observations are historical. Run a scan or include Unknown. Do not confuse a filter result with loss of saved data.

docs.title: Windows asks about firewall access
docs.text:
Windows rules can depend on the executable's full path and network profile. Moving a portable build can change which rule applies. An installed fixed-path build and a changing PR-build folder are not equivalent.

Read the prompt and allow access only if you trust the app and understand the requested network scope. Managed PCs may require an administrator. Missing devices or a discovery timeout alone does not prove firewall blocking. FingVibe has no delivered one-click firewall setup feature.

docs.title: Saved data cannot be loaded
docs.text:
1. Close all FingVibe instances.
  2. Preserve the whole data folder.
  3. Record the exact error and app version.
  4. Check disk space and folder permissions.
  5. Restore a known good backup only after preserving the current copy.
  6. Report the problem if the cause remains unclear.

Some editors are disabled after a failed load to protect unreadable data. Do not overwrite the file with an empty inventory or substitute stale legacy JSON.

If a save reports a conflict from another app instance, close duplicate instances and reload the current data before retrying. A save error is not success.

docs.title: Import skips data
docs.text:
Check that the workbook is .xlsx, has the expected sheet/MAC column, and meets the size limits. All duplicate-MAC rows are skipped. Missing or ambiguous person/room names skip those assignment fields.

Create or correct the managed entries, then Analyze again. The original IP and Fing state are not Online evidence. See Import from Fing.

docs.title: The speed test does not start
docs.text:
Read the WebView2 or connection error. Check that Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime is available and working. Use Microsoft's official WebView2 download/repair route rather than an untrusted runtime bundle.

Check access to speed.cloudflare.com, and finish other network measurements. VPNs, proxies, security policy, or connectivity can affect this optional tool. Retrying a test may consume substantial internet data; review the disclosure. LAN scanning does not require a successful speed test.

docs.title: DNS or traceroute has missing responses
docs.text:
An unanswered router or hop may block diagnostic responses while passing normal traffic. Windows DNS can answer from cache. A VPN may change the route. Compare independent checks instead of treating one missing response as proof.

See Network troubleshooting.

docs.title: A name, OS, or device type is wrong
docs.text: Inspect How this device was identified. Unknown and likely classifications are intentional when evidence is limited. Save a manual correction in Device details. A generic vendor or open service alone is not reliable OS proof.

docs.title: A backdrop or table option looks different
docs.text:
Windows transparency/high-contrast settings can override decorative appearance. Unsupported materials fall back to Solid. Check Compact rows, visible/combined columns, and Windows text size. See Settings.

If these steps do not explain the problem, use the support checklist.

docs.title: Scheduled scans and discoveries
docs.text: Scheduled scans are optional. They are off by default. They use the network selected in the shared Network: picker.

docs.title: Enable a schedule
docs.text:
1. Select the intended network.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Find Scheduled scans.
  4. Turn scheduling on.
  5. Choose 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, or 4 hours.
  6. Read the status sentence for the next approximate scan time.

The default interval is one hour. The first scheduled scan waits one full interval after enabling or loading. Changing the interval restarts that wait; it does not immediately run a scan.

docs.title: Keep the app open
docs.text:
Scheduling works while FingVibe is open, including when minimized. There is no separate Windows service, tray worker, or closed-app scheduler. Closing the app stops scheduling.

Windows sleep pauses scheduling. After resume, the app waits a full interval. It does not run missed scans to fill the gap. The shared header explains that scheduling operates while the app is open.

docs.title: Cancel or retry
docs.text:
Use Cancel scan to stop an active scheduled scan. Normal user cancellation waits a full interval before the next attempt. Turning scheduling off or closing the app stops scheduled work. Already committed checkpoint observations remain saved as incomplete.

LAN scans cannot overlap speed tests, troubleshooting, or device-service probes. If the app is busy, the network is unavailable, or a scan/save fails, Settings shows the reason and retry time. Retry waits grow up to the chosen interval.

These scans have the same evidence limits as manual scans. No response between samples does not establish continuous absence.

docs.title: New-device discoveries
docs.text:
After a successfully completed and saved scan, FingVibe can show an in-app popup for newly observed devices. It links to their details.

The first successful scan of a previously unknown network establishes a baseline and is quiet. Later first local discoveries can alert, including devices previously imported as Fing Only. Returning known devices do not repeatedly alert.

Discoveries made while minimized are combined and shown when you restore FingVibe. There is currently no Windows notification or notification archive. Cancelled, failed, or restored scans do not create discovery alerts.

If Windows network identity is unavailable, FingVibe explains why discoveries cannot be scoped reliably. A save error also prevents the popup.

The current screenshot set does not show the schedule card or discovery popup. They require state-specific native captures; see Visual coverage.

docs.title: Screenshot sources
docs.text: Screenshots in this manual are real native Windows captures, not mockups. They are illustrative UI evidence, not a real user's LAN or measurements.

docs.title: Initial manual captures
docs.text:
The new docs/screenshots/manual/ images come from Actions run 42532149572, attempt 1, artifact native-Full-capture-42532149572-attempt-1. The capture execution succeeded on a disposable Windows runner on 2026-11-08.

Application source: 6082b982af7ca5892072c9c09d6a8e9d8e8ff744. Validation harness source: 2ed22d5293c485aff171304bf561e90a7bbbfa48. These are different revisions and are not presented as one source. There is no application-source difference between the capture's revision and release v1.1.107 (0dbac6d9ee20dffba2015e4e4096b9482183e3dc).

The executable was stamped as v0.0.9 TEST, not an official release. The title, amber ribbon, About version, runner hostname, and test status messages are left visible. Do not infer a release version from their displayed values. The screen state follows baseline scan/cancellation/filter checks.

Every new image is 1280 x 800 pixels, copied unchanged. The safe context uses loopback 127.0.0.1, invented MAC data, sample public IP 203.0.113.10, and synthetic people/import information. No real LAN was scanned or private inventory loaded for this manual. No Cloudflare speed measurement was started.

Manual image Artifact image Visible state overview.png fingvibe-overview.png Summary of retained sample results. network.png fingvibe-network.png Sample network/provider identity. devices.png fingvibe-ui-review.png One responding review device; expanded filters. devices-empty.png fingvibe-devices-empty.png Search with no matching rows. device-details.png fingvibe-device-details.png Address/identity and assignment/category cards. people.png fingvibe-people.png Synthetic person entry. person-details.png fingvibe-person-details.png Synthetic entry with no assigned devices. settings.png fingvibe-settings.png Appearance and upper table options. import.png fingvibe-fing-import.png Synthetic workbook and analysis, not final import success. sql.png fingvibe-sql-editor.png Query ready to run, not a completed report. network-checks.png fingvibe-troubleshooting.png Ready-state controls; review-mode probes disabled. speed-test.png fingvibe-speed-test.png Gauges waiting for measurements. about.png fingvibe-about.png Test-build identity and source links.

All selected images were inspected for readable page content, safe sample data, and the state described above. They remain committed after the artifact expires.

docs.title: Earlier diagram image
docs.text:
The complete troubleshooting diagram uses the existing docs/screenshots/network-troubleshooting.png, a 1920 x 971 native capture supplied by iricigor on 2026-11-01. Its application version/source commit were not supplied and remain unknown.

Seven opaque regions redact network-specific values with the user's approval. All other pixels are preserved. It is a ready state: no checks had run. The diagram is illustrative, not discovered physical topology.

Detailed earlier-image provenance remains in the original screenshot record.

docs.title: Remaining visual coverage
docs.text:
The initial set shows the main pages and tool entry workflows. It does not show every scroll position or interaction:

Gap Why it is not illustrated yet Schedule controls and discovery popup The available complete capture set does not include these state-specific views. Lower identification editor, service results, and history summary They are below the device-details screenshot's viewport; a separate scoped capture is needed. Import conflict decisions and completed SQL rows Available new images show initial analysis/ready states, not those later states. Room editing and combined-column/schedule Settings controls The selected images focus on representative upper content rather than every equivalent control. Completed internet measurements A live speed test consumes data and reports results; no such run was performed for documentation. Activity grid and completed-observation table These controls are disabled in the documented release and must not be illustrated as currently usable.

Text instructions cover available behavior in these areas. Do not fabricate result images to fill a gap.

docs.title: Reproduce or replace
docs.text:
Use disposable Windows CI and the repository's native capture tooling. Request appropriate scenarios such as Devices, Overview, Network, DeviceDetails, People, PersonDetails, Settings, FingImport, SqlEditor, Troubleshooting, SpeedTest, and About. Use synthetic fixtures and keep measurements stopped.

Inspect the downloaded image, commit only the intended safe PNG, and update this record and the page caption with the actual source revision/run/state. Do not assume a newer screenshot automatically depicts a released feature.

docs.title: Appearance and table settings
docs.text:
Open Settings. Appearance changes apply immediately and are saved for your next launch. Read any save warning before assuming a choice was stored.

Native test-build screenshot. Combined-column and schedule settings continue below the visible area. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: Choose appearance
docs.text:
1. Select Mode: Light or Dark.
  2. Select a Theme.
  3. Select a Window backdrop.

Light mode offers Standard, Warm, and Colorful. Dark mode offers Standard, True Black (OLED), and Colorful. Changing mode keeps Standard or Colorful; Warm and True Black map to each other.

Backdrop choices are Solid, Mica, Mica Alt, and Acrylic. Solid shows the theme colors most directly. Windows transparency settings and platform support affect material backdrops. If a backdrop is unavailable, the app uses a solid background without forgetting your selection.

On first launch without a saved preference, the app follows Windows app mode. A saved preference takes precedence. Ordinary Windows light/dark changes do not switch FingVibe's theme while it is running.

Windows high contrast takes precedence over decorative colors. The app also respects Windows animation preferences for supported effects.

docs.title: Choose device columns
docs.text:
Find Devices page in Settings.

Visible columns controls which optional columns appear. Name and IP address are always shown. Combined columns places related values in one table column.

For example, IP/MAC places the IP above the MAC. Person/Room stacks the two assignments. If only one member is visible, it remains a normal column. Combined columns keep their applicable sort actions.

Resize columns from Devices. Separate and combined widths are remembered independently.

docs.title: Row density and previews
docs.text:
Compact rows uses less vertical space. Turn it off for Standard/relaxed rows. Both layouts can grow to accommodate larger text.

Cell hover previews reveals full shortened values after a short pointer pause. Keyboard focus exposes the full values too. Turning previews off restores ordinary value tooltips. Service, status, and explanation tooltips remain available.

docs.title: Reset columns
docs.text:
Reset columns restores default column visibility, combinations, and widths. It does not reset row density, hover-preview choice, or the saved Status filter. Use Clear filters on Devices to clear filtering.

If preferences cannot be loaded, Settings reports the problem and protects the unreadable file from being overwritten. See Common problems.

Scheduled scans are configured separately in Scheduled scans and discoveries.

docs.title: Speed test
docs.text:
The speed test measures this PC's internet connection, not transfer speed between your LAN devices. It uses Cloudflare.

Internet data use

A test can transfer more than 1 GB on a fast connection. FingVibe does not impose a data cap. Review the disclosure before every run, especially on a metered or mobile connection. Results are reported to Cloudflare.

docs.title: Run a test
docs.text:
1. Open Tools > Speed test.
  2. Finish or cancel any other active network measurement.
  3. Choose Start test.
  4. Read the data-use and Cloudflare reporting disclosure.
  5. Confirm only if you want to use that data and send the results.
  6. Wait for the completed result, or choose Cancel.

Native test-build ready state. No live test was run for this screenshot, and no measured result is implied. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: Read the measurements
docs.text:
Download measures receiving data from the internet. Upload measures sending data. Both are shown in Mbps: megabits per second, not megabytes per second.

HTTP latency is the measured delay for the engine's web requests. It is different from a LAN device's ping response.

Gauge values during the run are provisional estimates. Use the completed result for the final measurement. The gauge scale is logarithmic: equal visual spacing does not mean equal increments in Mbps. Numeric values remain the important readings.

The provider location is shown as unavailable when the engine does not supply it. The app does not guess a serving location.

docs.title: Cancellation and failures
docs.text:
Cancel, leaving the page, and closing the app use the same stop path. A cancelled run is not a completed result. If an error occurs, read the message before retrying.

Windows chooses the internet route. The LAN scanner's selected adapter does not bind this test. Wi-Fi signal, VPNs, other downloads, and provider conditions can change measurements.

The test needs Microsoft Edge WebView2 and access to https://speed.cloudflare.com. LAN scanning can work even when this optional tool cannot. See Speed test problems.

Only Cloudflare testing is available here. Azure testing remains deferred; it is not an alternative button or configuration. See Privacy for the requests involved.

docs.title: SQL reports
docs.text: The SQL editor reads saved inventory and history. SQL is a query language for asking questions about data. You can start with a built-in example without writing a query yourself.

docs.title: Run an example
docs.text:
1. Open Tools > SQL editor.
  2. Expand Schema and examples.
  3. Read an example and choose Use example.
  4. Choose Run.
  5. Read the result columns and the status message.
  6. Choose Cancel if you need to stop the query.

Safe test-build capture. No result rows are shown in this ready state. Screenshot sources.

A schema describes available tables/views and columns. Use the listed reporting views, whose names start with r_. They are more suitable than internal storage tables.

docs.title: A simple equipment report
docs.text:
This example lists current saved assignments, not human presence:

SELECT a.device_kind, a.device_id,
       p.name AS person, r.name AS room
FROM r_assignments a
LEFT JOIN r_people p ON p.person_id = a.person_id
LEFT JOIN r_rooms r ON r.room_id = a.room_id;

LEFT JOIN keeps a device's assignment row even if a person or room is missing. NULL means a missing value, not the word "NULL" stored as a name.

docs.title: What the editor can and cannot do
docs.text:
The editor accepts one read-only SELECT statement, including supported common table expressions. It cannot edit, delete, attach, or create databases. Unsupported commands and functions produce an error.

It reads a consistent snapshot of persisted data. It does not read unsaved drafts or continuously changing scanner objects. A committed partial scan can update saved aggregates, but r_scan_history contains completed-scan history only.

Limit What to expect 5 seconds A query that exceeds the time budget reports an error. 1,000 rows More rows produce explicit result truncation. 1 MiB of results Oversized results stop at a whole-row boundary with feedback. 64 columns Wider requests fail explicitly. Long cell values The UI can shorten previews separately from result completeness.

Do not treat a truncated result as the full dataset. Use a narrower query, selected columns, or a WHERE condition.

Missing inventory, a busy database, or invalid SQL is an error, not an empty successful report. Let a save finish before retrying a busy query. Leaving the tool or closing the app cancels pending work.

docs.title: Advanced reporting
docs.text:
MAC and virtual identities are different kinds of records. Summing both can count overlapping evidence twice. Stored observation times are not a continuous availability log.

For reporting views, exact limits, timestamp rules, and safe joins, use the SQL reporting reference.

docs.title: Version and support
docs.text:
Open Tools > About FingVibe to identify the running application. The page shows version, build kind, build time, and commit when available. Source, build, and creator links open in your browser.

The values identify the screenshot's test build, not your installation. Screenshot sources.

docs.title: Release versus test build
docs.text:
Official releases come from GitHub Releases. They do not show a test-build ribbon.

PR artifacts are experimental builds and show the PR identity. Other test builds show TEST; local developer builds show DEV. Acknowledging the diagonal ribbon hides it until closing the app. The title and About page still retain build identity.

If metadata is missing, the app says it is unavailable rather than guessing. A Release compilation setting alone does not make a build an official release.

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text:
1. Check Common problems.
  2. Search the existing issues.
  3. Open the bug-report form.
  4. Include the app version/build identity and Windows version.
  5. Describe the steps, expected result, actual result, and exact error.
  6. Include a privacy-safe screenshot if it helps.

For scan problems, say which kind of adapter you used, whether the scan finished, whether a VPN was active, and whether filters were applied. Compare identities rather than posting only different device totals.

Do not upload your inventory database, private Fing workbook, credentials, unredacted names/addresses, or router login details. See Privacy.

docs.title: Request a feature
docs.text: Use the same issue chooser and explain the problem you want to solve. Describe the desired outcome and a practical example. Maintainers organize requests into the repository's Epic backlog; submitting a request does not mean it is approved or scheduled.

docs.title: Documentation corrections
docs.text: Report the page link, the unclear/outdated sentence, and the app version. Screenshots with a test label may use sample values; that alone is not a bug. Incorrect workflow instructions or inaccessible visuals are useful findings.
